feedback: Approve. The candidate matches the iteration 6 design exactly: sensors at x = ±0.032 m with 0.016 m footprints, antisymmetric weights (-1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6), kp 3.0, ki 0.30, kd 0.40, base_speed 1.5, and line_loss last_direction. Iteration 6 is the best raced design (score 372.74, 19 of 20 oval finishes, oval max_error 0.042, oval line-loss events 0.25). Every later single-variable test lowered the score: kd 0.50 (iteration 8, 352.73), base_speed 1.3 (iteration 7, 269.51), kp 3.25 (iteration 9, 306.17), and the wider ±0.040 m spread (iteration 10, 267.93). Iteration 10 had oval finishes drop from 19 to 10 and left s-bend and slalom off track in every run. No other candidate has evidence at least as strong, and this is the final iteration, so no further revision can be tested before the unseen-track race. I make no claim about how this design will perform on that track. The main uncertainty is generalisation to a different shape, which I cannot measure from the development data. Approving the proven design is the only option that keeps a valid, well-tested build in the final race.
requested_changes: No field changes: race the approved build unchanged. The values are the iteration 6 design, which is the best raced candidate (372.74).
